title: The Dedication of the Lateran (9 November)
hookLine: the pope's own cathedral, mother of all churches

cards: Quick question: what's the pope's cathedral? Most people say Saint Peter's: it's the biggest, it's where the pope says the big Masses, it's on every postcard. But it's the wrong answer.
The pope is the bishop of Rome, and the bishop of Rome's cathedral is across the city, in a quieter neighborhood near the old walls: the Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran.
Carved on its front, in Latin, is a claim no other church makes. And on the ninth of November, every Catholic parish in the world keeps the birthday of this one building.

teach.b: The land once belonged to a Roman family, the Laterani, and then to the emperor.
After Constantine made Christianity legal, he gave the property to the bishop of Rome, and a basilica was built and dedicated in the early 300s, traditionally by Pope Sylvester.
It was the first great public church in the city.
For roughly a thousand years the popes lived next door, in the Lateran Palace, until they moved to Avignon in the 1300s, and five ecumenical councils met there.
The full name is the Archbasilica of the Most Holy Savior and of Saints John the Baptist and John the Evangelist.

teach.h: MOTHER AND HEAD OF ALL CHURCHES.
teach.b: The inscription on the front calls it the mother and head of all the churches of the city and of the world. That's why the feast is kept everywhere. It isn't about Roman architecture; it's about belonging.

teach.h: THE REAL BUILDING IS THE PEOPLE.
teach.b: Every parish, in Lagos or Lima or Little Rock, is connected to this one, through its bishop, to the bishop of Rome.
The feast ranks high enough that when the ninth of November falls on a Sunday, it replaces the ordinary Sunday.

teach.h: KNOW YOU NOT, THAT YOU ARE THE TEMPLE OF GOD?
teach.b: The Gospel for the day is Jesus driving the sellers out of the Temple, and the second reading is Paul's question to Corinth, in the Douay-Rheims: "Know you not, that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?"
The feast does what that line does. It honors a building, then turns around and says: the real building is the people.

how: Catholics everywhere keep the feast of the Dedication of the Lateran Basilica on 9 November, the cathedral of the bishop of Rome; when it falls on a Sunday it replaces the Sunday in Ordinary Time.

games.q: this year, 9 November falls on a Sunday. you're planning the parish Mass. what do you celebrate?
games.why: the feast ranks high enough to replace the ordinary Sunday: every parish keeps the mother church's birthday.

practice: Picture the church you know best, or the one nearest you: the doors, the smell, the light through the windows. Then picture the people: the usher, the choir, the family that's always late, the old man in the back pew.
If you pray, pray for that church and those people by name; if you don't belong to a parish, picture any community you belong to.

wordCard.voice: Lateran. The family name behind the land Constantine gave the bishop of Rome, and the name of his own cathedral, dedicated in the early 300s. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: mother and head — from the inscription on the Lateran's front.

carryVoice: Your line: the mother church. Every parish, everywhere, is tied to it. Day six hundred eighty-seven, done.
